summary: The human side is now the team's biggest risk. The plan is strong, but the key calls were deferred to AI (CLAUDE.md:74-75), and the team's own doc says the idea came from the AI council. Last year's semifinal instructions make this a scored test: every member had to speak and explain how they contributed value, no new strategy was allowed, and the written answers had to be in an authentic team voice. One person is leader, only trader, only student committer (98 of 98 student commits), runs all 10 routines on his Mac, gets every alert and submits. The leader cannot be replaced. The 16 Oct commit reversed the 15 Oct brief's first action within a day. One person changed the team rule so the AI may edit all three deliverables as [AI] suggestions, with no team vote recorded, and START_HERE.md still says the team writes everything, so the rule files now contradict each other. Nobody owns the numbers. The $294,453 vs $298,624 ladder-cost conflict comes from method, not error. The number sheet prices idealised zero-coupon bonds that mature on each 1 Jan payment date (I reproduced it exactly). The WInS holdings mature 2 weeks to 10.5 months earlier, which gives about $297.8k-$298.6k. The ~$298k / ~$1.4-2.2k room is the right figure for the IPS and the IBTR reflection, and the '1 in 3' odds understate the top-up risk. The calendar is tight. Every deadline falls on a Saturday morning in Sydney: the TNA ends Knox Term 4 week 2, the IPS ends week 4, and the Final Report is due two days after term ends. HSC exams run 13 Oct-5 Nov, and whether any member sits them is unverified. The fix is not more AI reports (about 745,000 words already). It is eight short meetings, real roles with backups, a team charter for decision rights, one student-owned numbers sheet, and an evidence ledger ('no artefact, no story'), because last year's doc shows comments telling the team to make up stories.

findings.title: Nobody owns the numbers: $294,453 vs $298,624 ladder cost on the same 15 Oct curve (reason and which to use)
findings.problem: Two AI pipelines a day apart gave two headline costs. The number sheet discounts each $50k to its 1 Jan payment date (idealised zero-coupon bonds, the 27 Sep STRIPS-era method); I reproduced $294,453 exactly. The WInS holdings mature 2 weeks to 10.5 months before the payment dates. Pricing at those maturities on the same curve and method gives $297,841, and L08 gives $297,778 forward and $298,624 on a yields-unchanged basis. About $3.4k of the gap is from maturity dates and $0.8k from the forward vs unchanged convention. For Laura's real WInS-only ladder (6 Oct email) and the IBTR note's basis, use about $298k with about $1.4-2.2k (5-8bp) of room. The $294k / $5.5k figure is valid only together with the number sheet's separate reinvestment section, and its '1 in 3' top-up odds are anchored to $294k, so they understate the risk (L08 rough model about 45%). The optimistic figure is now in the AI's 'Current status'. The maths is right on both sides; the failure is that no student owns one basis.
